s.q: Sum of n terms of an AP
s.d: Write $S_n$ forwards and backwards and add: each pair sums to $a+l$, $n$ pairs, so $2S_n=n(a+l)$.

s.n: If $S_n$ is quadratic in $n$ with no constant term, the series is an AP with $d=2\times$(coefficient of $n^2$).

s.f: A=\frac{a+b}2;\qquad n\ \text{AMs between } a,b:\ d=\frac{b-a}{n+1},\ \ \sum A_i=n\cdot\frac{a+b}{2}

s.d: For $\sum n^2$: sum $(k+1)^3-k^3=3k^2+3k+1$ from $k=1$ to $n$; telescope: $(n+1)^3-1=3\sum k^2+3\sum k+n$.

s.q: Sum of first n odd numbers and their squares

s.n: If differences of successive terms form an AP, $T_n$ is quadratic in $n$; if they form a GP, $T_n=ar^{n}+b$.
Rule: $\sum$ of products of $r$ consecutive integers $=\frac{\text{(last product)}\times(\text{next integer})}{r+1}$.
If $a,b,c$ in AP then $ka,kb,kc$ and $a+k,b+k,c+k$ are AP; if in GP then $\log a,\log b,\log c$ are in AP.
